Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our internal procurement and legal review, I'm attaching Qurex's redlines for the Master Services Agreement, the Data Processing Addendum, and an updated SOW with the integration milestones and acceptance criteria called out. High-level asks from our side: \n- Liability cap: move to 2x fees for first year and carve back for security incidents with 12-month lookback;
- Data residency / subprocessor transparency: we need an explicit list of subprocessors for any hosted inference;
- Audit rights: 1 per year with 30-day notice;
- SOW: more granular acceptance tests for model accuracy and latency SLAs in staging.

Attached: Qurex_MSA_Redlines.pdf (pdf, 182KB); Qurex_DPA_v1_redlines.docx (docx, 68KB); Qurex_SOW_draft_v3.docx (docx, 95KB).

We'd like to close commercial & legal review this month if possible — our procurement window is tight. Are you able to share Redwood's comments by EOD Tuesday?

Regards,
Oliver Grant
VP Partnerships | Qurex.ai

Karthik / Laura — forwarding Qurex's redlines and my read: the SOW's acceptance criteria look reasonable but the performance SLA thresholds may need clarifying around tokenized latency (p99 measurement window). From a CS standpoint, they're asking for a staged rollout and an integration window that aligns with Redwood Dedicated availability — we should confirm host model options and whether they require Dedicated or Hosted.

Laura, specific items I'd like your guidance on: 
- Liability cap: can we offer 1.5x for year 1 as a compromise (with carveouts for security incidents and prescribed remediation)?
- Audit rights: agree to annual audit limited to SOC2-type scope; need to limit vendor’s right to perform disruptive on-site activities.
- DPA: confirm that our standard subprocessor notification (portal + 30 days) satisfies their ask.

I'm happy to take point on operational details with Qurex if Legal gives the green light on these approaches. Suggest a 30-minute sync at 10:30 PT if that helps.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Partnerships Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@qurex.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Qurex — draft redlines (MSA / DPA / SOW)

Oliver — thanks for sending these over and apologies for the delay. I've reviewed Qurex's redlines and provided inline comments on the MSA and DPA. Summary of Redwood's positions and proposed compromise items: 

1) Liability cap: Redwood can accept a one-time concession to 1.5x fees for the first year only (capped to amounts paid in that year), contingent on mutual indemnities and excluding willful misconduct and gross negligence.

2) Subprocessors / data residency: We will provide a subprocessor registry and detailed subprocessor descriptions in the onboarding packet. For data residency: we cannot guarantee regionalized inference unless customer purchases Dedicated or Private; we will include an explicit note in the SOW clarifying deployment options and costs.

3) Audit rights: Redwood will accept annual audit rights limited to SOC2 evidence and remote collection methods; on-site audits will require 60 days' notice and are limited to exceptional cases with mutual NDA.

4) SOW acceptance / SLAs: We propose defining performance acceptance as p95 latency < X ms for the agreed test harness, with p99 included as an escalation metric. We'll add a staging signoff milestone and a 30-day post-launch observation window.

Next steps: 
- I'm attaching a tracked-changes version of the MSA/DPA (see attachments) with the specific language.
- Karthik/Marissa: please confirm commercial terms (term length, initial committed capacity, and billing cadence) so I can include the values in the SOW.

If Qurex is ok with the 1.5x compromise and the remote-audit approach, we can prepare an execution-ready package and circulate for signatures this week. Alternatively, if they insist on 2x and unrestricted audits we'll need to escalate to execs.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_MSA_comments_Qurex.pdf (pdf, 24KB); Redwood_DPA_comments_Qurex.pdf (pdf, 12KB)
